text:
matt: FYI hitting a weird client-resume case in the sampleapp where resumed streams sometimes start with junk bytes and the client parser treats it as a new chunk boundary, producing garbled JSON.
priya: ugh. can you repro reliably? which SDK + runtime?
matt: node sdk (fetch polyfilled) in the sample app running behind our local dev proxy. reconnect flow: client aborts then reconnects with Last-Event-ID header. ~10% of reconnects return a `\u0000\u0000` prefix before the first event. logs:```[info] reconnect start id=abc123
[recv] 0x00 0x00 0x1b 0x7b 0x22  -> invalid chunk prefix
[parser] json parse error: Unexpected token "\u0000"
```
ron: hmm could be proxy clipping/leftover buffer. does it only happen when proxy warmup (first request after idle)?
matt: yes seems correlated with pool warmup on the proxy side, and only when we had fast aborts earlier. not seen on direct host.
alice: can you paste the fetch options? maybe `keepalive` or a nonstandard header is confusing it.
matt: client code:```const ac = new AbortController(); fetch(url, { headers: { 'Last-Event-ID': id }, signal: ac.signal });``` nothing fancy. workaround we used: on resume, trim leading non-UTF8 bytes before feeding to the SSE parser (hacky).
priya: we should narrow whether it's our runtime or the proxy; matt can you repro with curl to the dedicated endpoint (no proxy)?
matt: tried curl -> no prefix. direct request clean. so proxy is suspect. repro steps added to sampleapp README.
devex-bot: New issue created: DEX-1137 "streaming: proxy can emit leading null bytes on resume causing parser errors". (link: https://tracker/redwood/DEX-1137) :spiral_note_pad: 
sre-oncall: tagging eng-infra since proxy warmup looks like a resource reuse bug, assigning to @ron. can you collect raw tcp captures next time?
ron: will capture tcpdump on next repro and also try with `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` vs. content-length to see if framing differs.
alice: also add a defensive client-side parser change: ignore leading 0x00..0x1f bytes until a valid event start (log when trimming) — should be safe and buys time.
matt: thanks — I'll add the client-side trim + test vector and attach pcap when ron has it.
priya: nice plan. small thread but good find. :thumbsup:
